title: New Maruti Suzuki Baleno: What is really new in India's largest-selling premium hatchback?- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Maruti Suzuki Baleno 2026 adds Level 2 ADAS, ventilated seats, a Z12E engine and design changes.   September 07, 2026 / 18:28 IST             The new Maruti Suzuki Baleno brings several additions over the outgoing model, led by Level 2 advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and ventilated front seats. The premium hatchback also gets a new petrol engine, additional safety and convenience equipment, an updated front design and a new colour. Here is a closer look at everything that is new in the Baleno 2026. The most important addition is Level 2 ADAS, which is claimed to be a segment-first feature. The system uses a combination of radar and camera and offers eight driver assistance functions. These include adaptive cruise control, lane keep assist, lane departure prevention, lane departure warning, vehicle sway warning, advanced emergency braking, forward collision warning and high beam assist. The new Baleno also gets a tyre pressure monitoring system and an emergency stop signal. Other safety equipment includes six airbags, electronic stability programme, anti-lock braking system with electronic brakeforce distribution, hill hold control, reverse parking sensors, three-point seat belts and seat belt reminders. The Baleno now comes with ventilated front seats featuring leatherette upholstery. Maruti Suzuki claimed this is another first-in-segment feature. Other additions include a wireless smartphone charger with an active cooling function and a Clarion-branded sound system with Arkamys tuning. The 9-inch SmartPlay Pro+ touchscreen infotainment system, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, head-up display and 360-degree camera have been carried forward. Suzuki Connect continues to offer more than 40 connected-car features. The new Baleno is powered by a 3-cylinder Z12E petrol engine featuring idle start-stop technology and Dual VVT. It develops 82.93 PS and 112.4 Nm of peak torque. The engine is available with 5-speed manual and automated manual transmission options. Maruti Suzuki claimed a fuel efficiency of 23.80 kmpl for the manual version and 24.77 kmpl for the AGS version. These figures are 6.4 per cent and 7.9 per cent higher, respectively, than those of the outgoing model. The Baleno S-CNG also gets the Z12E engine, paired with a 5-speed manual gearbox. Its claimed efficiency stands at 33.61 km/kg, an improvement of 9.8 per cent over its predecessor. The design changes are largely concentrated at the front. The new Baleno gets a redesigned NEXWave grille with three-dimensional patterns and horizontal chrome elements. The grille is accompanied by a sculpted front bumper, a revised lower grille and a chrome fender garnish. A shark-fin antenna has also been introduced. The premium hatchback is available in seven colours, including the newly introduced Enigmatic Teal shade. As of now, Maruti Suzuki has announced the price of only the entry-level variant of the Baleno 2026. It starts at Rs 6.10 lakh (ex-showroom). Bookings for the new Baleno can be made for a token amount of Rs 11,000.                        Discover the latest  Business News ,  Sensex , and  Nifty  updates.
